Subject: Service moat topology — annotated demarcation & data-path labeling (SOC 2 / SIG evidence request)

Team / Greenline security,

Greenline asked for a compact "annotated demarcation" of our Dedicated/Private topology that highlights the service "moat" (control plane <> inference plane demarcation), labeled data-paths for ingress/egress, and a simple segmentation matrix they can include in their SIG submission. They'd like diagrams and a short narrative that maps controls to SOC 2 categories (primarily CC6/CC7) and calls out KMS boundaries and egress filters.

Request: can we produce a single annotated diagram (PNG) plus a segmentation matrix (xlsx) and a CSV with labeled data-paths? Aim for one page of narrative (250–400 words) and the three artifacts attached. Greenline is on a tight audit window — they asked for this by EOD Wednesday (2027-02-17).

Notes / constraints:
- This is focused on Dedicated + Private (VPC and on-prem) — do not include Hosted API flow other than a one-line fallback note.
- Explicitly mark what we consider "customer-managed" vs "Redwood-managed."
- Call out KMS/HSM boundary (customer-managed keys possible in Private deployments).

Kimberly / Karthik / Priyom — please coordinate who will draft the narrative and who will produce the diagram. Greenline security is looped for visibility; they may give quick follow-up Qs.

Thanks,

Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachments (stubs): service-moat-topology-v1.drawio.png (diagram stub), segmentation-matrix-v2.xlsx (matrix stub), data-path-labeling.csv (path list stub)

Subject: Re: Service moat topology — annotated demarcation & data-path labeling (SOC 2 / SIG evidence request)

Diego —

Attached is a first pass: service-moat-topology-v1.drawio.png and a draft segmentation-matrix-v2.xlsx. I labeled the control plane components (account management, model registry, routing) as "Redwood-managed" and inference nodes as "customer-data-plane" for Dedicated/Private. The moat annotation shows the following callouts:

- Control plane to inference plane: TLS mutual auth + service token routing (no persistent data in control plane)
- KV/prefix caches: local to inference pools, encrypted at-rest with node-level disk encryption (our default); for Private with customer KMS we annotate the external KMS boundary.
- Egress paths: defined per VPC egress rules and optional NAT/Gateway (we call these out in the matrix).

I left two open items for Karthik / Priyom to confirm:
1) Exact labeling for on-prem HSM integration (we currently support external PKCS#11 endpoints; confirm vendor specifics for Greenline).
2) Recommended retention/eviction behavior for KV caches (we state default TTL but need a security affirmation).

I can draft the short narrative (350 words) once Karthik confirms the HSM wording.

-Kim

--
Kimberly Park

Thanks Diego / Kim — first pass looks helpful. A couple clarifying Qs so we can map to our SIG: 

1) KMS boundary: can you confirm whether Redwood ever holds plaintext model inputs/outputs in the control plane? We need an explicit statement for SIG that control plane does not persist customer inference data.
2) Egress: do you have examples of egress rules per environment (Dedicated on AWS, Private on customer VPC)? A short example snippet or CIDR ranges would be helpful.
3) HSM: for our on-prem Private deployment we plan to present an HSM vendor and need to understand how Redwood integrates (pull vs push key wraps). Would appreciate a short note.

We can accept the artifacts in Drive or PDF. Our audit window is tight; having answers inline in the narrative makes our assessor's life easier.

Regards,
Maya Singh

Greenline Analytics

Maya / Greenline team —

Thanks for the quick review. Short answers and next steps (we updated the attachments and pushed to the Drive link):

1) Control plane persistence: Redwood does NOT persist customer inference payloads in the control plane. Routing metadata (request id, model id, timestamps) is logged for observability; payloads are forwarded to the inference pool and only stored in caches in encrypted form where configured. We will add the explicit statement to the narrative: "Redwood control plane does not persist cleartext customer inference inputs or outputs."

2) Egress examples: for Dedicated on AWS we provide recommended egress CIDR snippets tied to the VPC NAT/Gateway — see attached CSV data-path-labeling.csv (column: environment, component, egress_cidr_example). For Private (customer VPC) egress is driven by the customer's routing table; our best practice note is to restrict outbound to the customer-approved monitoring/registry endpoints and to Redwood-managed control plane addresses (we list examples in the CSV).

3) HSM integration: Redwood supports PKCS#11-compatible HSMs. Integration modes:
   - Pull mode: Redwood calls a customer-managed HSM endpoint (mutual-TLS) to unwrap keys at runtime.
   - Push mode: customer wraps keys and uploads the wrapped key material to Redwood via an encrypted channel — Redwood never receives unwrapped key material in this mode.

Karthik / Priyom — please confirm the HSM wording and KV cache TTL language; Kim will fold that into the final narrative.

Next steps:
- Kimberly to finalize the narrative and embed the explicit control-plane statement (EOD Wed).
- Diego to export artifacts to PDF and share the Drive link (done).
- Greenline to confirm any follow-up assessor questions by Thursday morning.

Diego Fernandez
